instance.note: Rubrics are verifier-only for this instance: they describe the abandoned layout-diagnostics overlay scaffolding by subsystem role, never by injected name, and accept any sound subtractive refactor that leaves the pre-feature crate intact.

rubrics.criterion: The abandoned overlay-feature wrapper is gone from the view layer: no wrapper view type, style/variant enum, style-derivation methods, descriptive constructor, or constructor free function of the feature survives, and no file dedicated to the feature remains under the views directory.
rubrics.rationale: The feature's rendering body lives in the library as a normal sibling view module; removing the whole wrapper cluster (including the file itself) rather than a shell of it is the central outcome of this instance's assigned smell.

rubrics.criterion: The public chaining convenience trait is back to its pre-feature method list: the member that was added so the overlay could be reached inline (the one accepting a style argument and forwarding into the wrapper) is removed together with the wrapper, and the trait's other chaining members stay as they were.
rubrics.rationale: The trait is the crate's primary user-facing composition API; a leftover forwarding member would keep advertising the dead capability on every view, which is exactly the surface-rot this task targets.

rubrics.criterion: The read-only helper members the feature pulled onto the shared state-owner type (the ones exposing layout rectangles for the overlay and counting the current dirty regions) are removed when their only consumer was the wrapper, without disturbing the state-owner's surrounding layout/dirty-region maintenance.
rubrics.rationale: These accessors exist solely to feed the overlay; they are invisible to the compiler once the wrapper is deleted, so removing them proves the sweep was usage-driven rather than error-driven.

rubrics.criterion: The paint-family constructor member that the overlay's styling derived from (the color-with-replaced-alpha helper) is removed along with the feature, leaving the paint type's other constructors unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: A single-caller paint helper is the easiest orphan to overlook because nothing breaks when it stays; its removal distinguishes a complete cleanup from a wrapper-only deletion.

rubrics.criterion: The command-name constant the feature reserved in the command module (the one the wrapper's command registration pushed and its event handling decoded) is removed, with the command module left otherwise as it was.
rubrics.rationale: The reserved registry name is the registration half of the never-wired toggle; leaving it behind keeps a dangling registry entry that misrepresents available commands.

rubrics.criterion: The cross-file wiring of the removal is complete and consistent everywhere: the view module registry in the library lists no declaration or glob re-export for the removed feature, and a workspace-wide search for the feature's names finds nothing outside the removal itself.
rubrics.rationale: Publishing and referencing are spread across files in this instance; the repair is only coherent if every wiring point — not only the feature's own module — is rewound in the same change set.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not include unrelated drive-by edits in the modules it touches: pre-existing members of the view module registry, the chaining trait, the state-owner implementation, the paint type, and the command module are byte-equivalent to the pre-feature state apart from the feature's own additions being deleted.
rubrics.rationale: This instance requires edits in several high-traffic core files; the temptation to tidy neighboring code while inside them is the natural way an otherwise correct repair picks up unrelated risk.

rubrics.criterion: No leftover scaffolding artifact remains that the compiler would have tolerated: no empty or stub module file, no kept-but-unregistered or registered-but-unhandled command plumbing, no orphan helper methods or constants, and no placeholder documentation or comment block referencing the removed feature.
rubrics.rationale: The distinguishing difficulty of this instance is exactly the set of removals nothing forces; a repair is finished only when the tolerated debris — not just the compile-breaking references — is gone.

rubrics.criterion: The feature is not kept alive or papered over instead of removed: no new example, gallery entry, test, forwarding shim, suppression attribute, or other artificial usage is introduced to make the scaffolding compilable or to preserve its names.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt's requirement is subtraction; in this instance the natural wrong turn is wiring the half-built feature into a demo or a stub so the names become technically used, which preserves the maintenance burden while hiding it.

rubrics.criterion: Every API item and member that existed before the feature still exists afterwards with the same name, signature, and semantics — including the crate's long-dormant pre-existing members that also look unused today.
rubrics.rationale: The crate carries latent API of its own; the task's boundary is the feature scaffolding only, so over-deletion of pre-existing members is the most plausible case-specific regression here.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not introduce any build or test failure: the library and its examples compile, and the library test suite passes, exactly as on the tree the repair started from.
rubrics.rationale: The removal is behavior-preserving by construction — nothing reachable changed — so any new compile error, dangling reference, or test failure indicates an incomplete or inconsistent repair rather than a necessary trade-off.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not alter the observable runtime behavior of remaining code: layout computation and caching, dirty-region marking, event dispatch, command enumeration, accessibility, and GC bookkeeping all keep their pre-feature implementations.
rubrics.rationale: Several removals sit inside the hottest core of the library (state owner, paint, modifier trait, command dispatch); a plausible sloppy repair 'simplifies' adjacent logic while deleting neighbors, which this item catches.
